lines.note: Continues the preceding page's discussion of having penetrated and understood letters or learning. The initial netrado is a divided-word continuation, not an independent word to be expanded here.

Doori wo tessuru means grasping a principle thoroughly; the Portuguese describes reaching its end through reason. The damaged vowel in printed ruzão remains provisionally as in the aligned OCR, rather than silently normalizing to razão.
Ao cabo completes chegar: reaching the end or fully comprehending the matter. This short continuation belongs to the preceding example.

runs.text: Coração de ferro, ou forte, & con-

lines.note: Tesshin is an iron heart, figuratively strong and steadfast. The Portuguese adjective constante is divided after con- at the physical line break.
Completes constante, steadfast. S. is the upright written-language usage label, rather than another italic word in the definition.
This second tesshin is an iron needle, explained by kurogane no hari. The initial is the same damaged T type as neighboring entries, not the OCR F; the large-needle gloss continues below.
Completes the tool definition: a large iron needle, lancet, or awl. These alternatives explain the instrument rather than the figurative heart sense above.
Tessho denotes reliable proof or testimony, matched by prova and testemunha verdadeira. The scan supports initial T instead of OCR F; the unaccented final o is retained.
Tessho funmyoo ni gozaru says there is clear proof. The scan supplies the omitted paragraph sign and initial T; pro- begins Portuguese prova on the next row.
Completes prova manifesta, manifest or evident proof. The preserved historical st form belongs to the Portuguese adjective, not to the Japanese example.

Teyari is a short hand-spear, glossed with geneta and a small lance. The e in pequena is weak in the impression but the surviving letter sequence supports the full word; OCR Goneta is corrected to the visible Geneta.

runs.text: Batel, ou eſquife de que ſe ſerue al-

lines.note: Teyasu names a boat or ship's skiff. The weak f has a surviving cross stroke, supporting the nautical eſquife rather than OCR eſquiſe; al- continues into algum below.

runs.text: gum nauio posto que no Cami ſe diz.

lines.note: Completes algum navio and explains that the skiff is called teuma in Cami, the upper regions. Nauio and Cami replace OCR natio and Cama; the regional name is Japanese within the Portuguese explanation.

The alternative faxifune, hashifune, is another name for the small boat. The abraded n is retained as the usable reading supported by the surviving type and nautical context; l is the Latin alternative marker.
Teyawaraka denotes gentleness or softness. The following teyawarakana is the attributive form, completed by hito on the next physical line.
Hito completes teyawarakana hito, a gentle or mild person. The Portuguese directly supplies those character qualities.
Teyawarakani is the adverbial form, gently or mildly. The printed Adu. identifies its function without repeating the preceding definition.
Teyoo denotes a movement or gesture of the hands. The scan shows initial T and a caron over the final o, correcting OCR reyǒ without changing the printed vowel mark.
Teyowai means weak or lacking force. The Portuguese contrasts effective strength with frailty; the historical printed fraxo is retained rather than regularized.
Teyowai bushi is a weak, cowardly soldier. Soldado is legible as one word despite the damaged letter area that produced OCR Solad o.
Teyowai dangi is an ineffectual sermon or discourse. The scan supplies the paragraph sign omitted by OCR; the Portuguese description continues below.
Completes the sermon definition: little substance and no vigor. Sustancia is the printed historical form and is not expanded to modern substância.

runs.text: Tempo, ou flor da idade em que hũ

lines.note: Tezakari names the period or prime of life when manual skill is at its best. Hũ begins the indefinite person who performs the work described below.

runs.text: faz bẽ algũa obra de mãos como eſcreuer, pin-

lines.note: The person does manual work well, with writing and painting among the examples. Faz corrects OCR far; pin- begins pintar on the next row.
Tar completes pintar, painting, followed by cutting and other manual activities. These examples complete the definition of the prime of manual skill.

runs.text: Obra dalgũa peſſoa engenhoſa de mã-

lines.note: Tezaiku is handiwork by someone ingenious with the hands. The scan supports peſſoa and engenhoſa rather than the OCR omissions; mã- continues as mãos below.

runs.text: os, que nãohe proprio official daquelle officio.

lines.note: Completes mãos and specifies a maker who is not a professional practitioner of that trade. The worn negative is read nãohe, retaining its close printed spacing rather than silently recasting the sentence.

Kore wa miga tezaiku ni itaita is translated as making this with one's own hand. Miga is the visible, somewhat abraded form rather than OCR niga; itaita is a historical past form and should not be modernized to itashita. The paragraph sign and Isto are visible.
Da minha mão completes the first-person translation, made by my own hand. The singular mão contrasts with the general plural mãos in the definition.
Tezawayakana describes something finely made and well finished. Prima is an assessment of excellent workmanship, not an ordinal numeral.
Polida completes the praise of the object as polished or refined. It belongs to the same adjective entry.
The adverbial form tezawayakani and nominal tezawayakasa follow the preceding adjective. Both are printed on one indented physical row; the damaged w-like u replaces the OCR n in the first form.

runs.text: O eſcreuer, ou fazer algũa couſa

lines.note: Tezusami is writing or doing something casually for amusement. The Portuguese verb is fazer, with f, not OCR ſazer; the contrast with deliberate purpose continues below.

runs.text: não de propoſito, mas por paßa tempo.

lines.note: Completes the pastime sense: not deliberately for a purpose, but to pass the time. The worn o in propoſito is restored from the visible word; paßa tempo preserves the printed historical spelling and separation.

Tezushi, alternatively tekugutsu, names puppet performance or the puppeteer's work. The scan and repeated Tezuxiuo below support z rather than OCR c in the first form. The comma before l is visible. Its normalized typography is not copied.

runs.text: fazer andar à roda, & menear bonifrates.

lines.note: The activity consists of making puppets go around and manipulating them. Andar and bonifrates correct the OCR ander and bonifraires; the Portuguese supplies the puppet sense of the Japanese terms.
Tezushi wo suru means performing the puppet activity. The additional sense identifies the practitioner himself; q̃ is the printed abbreviation for the relative pronoun.
Completes the practitioner sense: the person who carries out this trade. The final e of este is weak in the impression, but its remnant and the complete phrase support this reading over OCR est.

runs.text: O ar remeter, ou dar nos inimigos, &c.

lines.note: Tedzukai here denotes charging or striking at enemies. The headword is Tezzucai, not OCR Fezzueai. The first r of ar remeter is heavily abraded; the usable reading retains the locally aligned unusual separation rather than silently modernizing it.
Vide Te cross-refers to the Japanese entry te. A second sense then begins the layout or distribution of a building; reparti- continues into repartimento below.

runs.text: mento das caſas, ou edificio. Vt,

lines.note: Completes repartimento, the arrangement of houses or a building. Tedzukai begins the example of a well-planned house; the c is abraded but fits the surviving form repeated from the headword.
No yoi iye completes tedzukai no yoi ie, a house with a good layout. The Portuguese says it is well designed and begins repartida across the line break.
Completes repartida, well apportioned or arranged. The scan supports partida, replacing OCR puncida and closing the house-layout example.

runs.text: O tomar, ou afferrar com as mã-

lines.note: Tedzukami is taking hold of something directly with the hands. Mã- is the beginning of mãos across the physical line break.
Completes the definition as seizing something with the hands, then begins tedzukami ni suru wa. The Japanese topic-marked phrase receives its evaluation in the next row.

runs.text: O aferrar, ou tomar com as mãos co-

lines.note: Warui completes the judgment that grabbing with the hands is bad. The Portuguese explains the action, with co- continuing into como below; mãos corrects OCR nãos.

runs.text: mo com as vnhas he couſa que parece mal.

lines.note: Completes como and compares grasping with the hands to grasping with the nails, something that looks improper. He, que, parece, and mal restore legible Portuguese where the OCR produced nonsensical letter sequences.
Tedzukara is an adverb meaning by one's own hand or personally. The printed apropria spacing is retained and the alternative formulation continues below.

The gloss continues as by one's own hands, followed by tedzukara mono wo. The final o of the object-particle sequence is very faint near the right rule; monouo is the usable reading, with that abrasion retained as a caveat.

runs.text: Fazer algũa couſa com as proprias

lines.note: Itasu completes the example of doing something oneself. The Portuguese begins the same explanation; the faint final s supports proprias rather than the OCR's comma.
Mãos completes com as proprias mãos, by one's own hands. The very short row remains a separate continuation line.
Tedzukuri describes something made with one's own hands. The adjective proprias continues directly into mãos below.
Completes the literal handmade sense and gives tedzukuri ni suru, make by hand. Item introduces the figurative use developed on the next row.

The abbreviated per met signals a transferred or figurative use. Tedzukurina koto wo yuu is saying something of one's own invention, as the following Portuguese makes explicit; met corrects the OCR mer.

runs.text: couſas de ſeu marte, & propria inuẽção.

lines.note: Completes dizer: saying things from one's own resources and invention. De seu marte is the historical idiom, while the abbreviation in inuẽção remains unexpanded.

runs.text: O estar apertado, & poſto em mui-

lines.note: Tedzume describes being pressed or driven into straits. Mui- starts muita, qualifying the affliction on the next row.

runs.text: ta aflição, ou estar ja no cabo. ¶

lines.note: Completes muita aflição and adds being at the end of one's resources. Tezzu begins the example divided before meni on the next line; no hyphen is supplied where the print does not establish one.

Completes Tezzumeni natta, being brought to this constrained condition. Enlargement shows a narrow dotted i in meni, correcting OCR mena; the Portuguese describes being left in this state, with parado rather than OCR parade.
Tedzume no shoobu ni naru describes reaching a decisive contest. The abraded na ru is retained with the draft's visible separation; its interpretation is the verb naru, not two independent words.

runs.text: põto que não ſe pode deixar de ganhar, ou per

lines.note: The contest reaches a point where winning or losing cannot be avoided. Per continues as perder below, without an invented terminal hyphen; põto retains its printed nasal abbreviation.
Der completes perder, losing at play. This finishes the account of a contest brought to an unavoidable outcome.

runs.text: O ter deuer com alguem ajudando,

lines.note: Tedzuke is a connection with someone expressed through assistance. The historical phrase ter deuer is retained; the next row adds favoring or supporting the person.
Favoring or assisting completes the definition, and tedzuke wo suru supplies the example. The repeated headword has e rather than the OCR Tozzuqeuo.

runs.text: ¶ Item, Peßoa que hum cria, ou tem jun-

lines.note: A further sense is a person one raises or keeps close. Hum replaces OCR ham; jun- begins junto on the following row.
Completes junto de si, keeping the person near oneself. It remains part of the noun's second sense.
Tedzuke, tedzukeru, tedzuketa is the corresponding verb, to rear or train someone close to oneself. The worn Portuguese verb is criar, not OCR rlar; its construction continues below.
Completes the upbringing or domestication sense: keeping someone near oneself or making them tame. The historical domesticalo spelling and provisional st treatment are preserved.
Tedzutsu and tedzutsuna describe an inept person. The Latin l introduces the adjectival alternative; the relative clause explains the lack of skill below.

runs.text: não ſabe fazer nada: particularmente ſe diz

lines.note: The person cannot do anything, with a particular application to follow. The visible two-point punctuation after nada is retained as a colon rather than the OCR period.

runs.text: de hũa molher deſmazelada, & que não ſabe

lines.note: The dictionary particularly applies the term to a careless or inept woman. The worn e in deſmazelada is recoverable; the following line specifies household tasks.
Completes the historical household example: unable to do domestic tasks. This is the source's characterization, not an additional modern assessment.
Tedzuyoi means strong and effective. The repeated example begins Tez- in upright Japanese type; the visible terminal dash is a hyphen rather than the OCR period.
Tez- followed by the printed zu yoi fito forms tedzuyoi hito, a firm, strong, effective person. The internal spacing is retained; the Portuguese final eficaz has no securely visible added stop.
Tedzuyoi dangi is an effective sermon, contrasting with teyowai dangi in the first column. The paired example confirms that strength here can describe persuasive speech.
Tedzuyoo is the associated adverbial form, strongly or effectively. The circumflex is preserved as printed; this short derivative occupies its own indented row.
Tedzuyosa is the abstract noun for strength or effectiveness. The abraded second letter is e, matching the family above, rather than OCR Tozzuyoſa.

runs.text: Hũa medida como alqueire q̃ leua 10.

lines.note: To is a measure compared with the Portuguese alqueire and said to contain ten Japanese measures. The oversized initial T belongs to this headword and spans two rows; it is not a stray dash. Alqueire and 10 restore the legible measurement gloss.

runs.text: medidas de Iapão. Mas não ſe vſa per ſi ſe não

lines.note: Completes the quantity and explains that this measure-name is not normally used alone. The first two rows sit beside the enlarged T, which is included in the owning line's crop.

The term occurs in compounds, illustrated by itto, one to, and toate, a distribution or allowance by the to. The first example's damaged middle strokes are read Itto; the examples remain separate Japanese forms, not words within a Portuguese sentence.
This to means a door. To wo tatsuru, alternatively sasu, is supplied as the expression for closing it; the source's Japanese forms are retained.
The Portuguese translates the door-closing example, then toguchi begins a new illustration meaning doorway or entrance. Porta corrects OCR parta.
Da porta completes entrada da porta, the doorway. The short row continues the preceding definition and is not another entry.
To is explained by hoka, outside. The usage note says it is especially used in a particular context, completed below; the historical capital V in Vſa is preserved.
The context is going to the latrines, illustrated by to e mairu. Vai corrects OCR var; the right edge reads às, beginning the Portuguese translation without a line-end hyphen.
Latrinas completes the translation of to e mairu, going out to the latrines. The continuation is ordinary body text.
This to denotes a gulf or stretch of sea to be crossed. Golfo replaces the malformed OCR Goifro; va- starts the verb watasu in the example.

runs.text: Paſſar eſte golfão, ou mar que não tem

lines.note: Tasu completes to wo watasu, crossing that expanse of water. The Portuguese expands it as crossing a gulf or sea, with its physical description continuing below; the Japanese fragment is upright, not italic.

runs.text: da parte direita, & eſquerda porto, nem ſur-

lines.note: The water has no port or anchorage on the right or left. Parte and direita correct the OCR omissions and vowel confusion; ſur- begins surgidouro below.
Completes surgidouro, an anchorage or place where a vessel can lie. The short row closes the sea-crossing definition.

To, explained by toishi, is a whetstone for sharpening. The short unaccented headword and initial T of Toixi are supported by the print; aguçar corrects OCR aguças. The supplied NINJAL headword index independently confirms short To after the visual reading.
The whetstone sharpens razors, knives, and similar tools. Historical naualhas retains the printed u/v spelling.

Too is glossed as quickly or early; too tatsu illustrates leaving early. The circumflexes remain as printed, cedo replaces OCR caco, and Par- begins partir-se across the page boundary, anticipated by the catchword. The worn internal s-types of Depreſſa remain a local reading caveat.
Anticipates the opening tirſe cedo on f505, completing Par- across the page boundary. It is page furniture, not a second occurrence in running text.
